# UX & Error-Handling Checklist: Frontend Chat UI

**Purpose**: Validate the *requirements* (not the implementation) for interaction/loading states and
for cross-flow error-handling consistency, ahead of `/speckit-tasks` — a standard-depth pre-tasks
gate, self-review by the author.
**Created**: 2026-08-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) (also referencing [plan.md](../plan.md)/[research.md](../research.md)
for traceability only — every item below tests requirement quality, not code or design decisions)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context
and requirements. Focus areas selected: UX/interaction states, error-handling & failure-mode
consistency.

## Requirement Completeness — Interaction & Loading States

- [x] CHK001 Is the visible/announced difference between the transient "checking" moment before the
      first `GET /documents` response and the deliberate empty-corpus state specified, so the two
      are never conflated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008/FR-009] — **Fixed**: FR-008 now requires the
      initial-loading moment to be visually distinct from FR-009's empty state.
- [x] CHK002 Is a minimum or maximum visible duration for the chat loading indicator specified,
      preventing a flash of a loading state for an answer that resolves near-instantly? [Gap, Spec
      §FR-006] — **Fixed**: FR-006 now requires no indicator flash for a near-instant response.
- [x] CHK003 Does the spec define what happens to the question text already typed in the input while
      a previous question is still pending — is it cleared, retained, or blocked from further
      editing? [Gap, Spec §FR-001/FR-006] — **Fixed**: FR-001 clears the input on submit; FR-006
      disables it while pending.
- [x] CHK004 Is the exact wording or content requirement for the sidebar's empty state specified
      (beyond "explicit"), so two independent readings of the spec couldn't produce visibly
      different results? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009] — **Fixed**: FR-009 now requires the empty state to
      explain no documents exist yet and point at the upload control.
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for what a user sees between confirming a document upload
      selection and the upload actually starting (e.g. filename shown, or nothing until it
      completes)? [Gap, Spec §FR-010] — **Fixed**: FR-010 now states the upload starts immediately on
      selection, with no separate confirmation step.

## Requirement Clarity — Interaction & Loading States

- [x] CHK006 Is "prevent submitting a blank or whitespace-only question" (FR-004) clarified as to
      whether the send control is visibly disabled versus silently ignoring a click/Enter — two
      different observable behaviors both satisfying the literal text? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004] —
      **Fixed**: FR-004 now requires the send control to be visibly disabled.
- [x] CHK007 Is the mechanism for indicating the 1000-character limit "before the request is sent"
      (FR-005) specified as live/real-time feedback while typing versus feedback only at submit
      time? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005] — **Fixed**: FR-005 now requires continuous feedback as the user
      types, once over the limit.
- [x] CHK008 Is "disable the send control" (FR-006) scoped explicitly to the send button, the text
      input, or both, during a pending request? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006] — **Fixed**: FR-006 now
      explicitly disables both the input and the send control.
- [x] CHK009 Are the hover-triggered sidebar actions (download, delete — FR-013/FR-015) and the
      always-clickable citation-badge download action (FR-013) reconciled as an intentionally
      different interaction model for the same underlying capability, or is this an unaddressed
      inconsistency? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013/FR-015] — **Fixed**: FR-013 now requires the
      sidebar's hover actions to also be reachable by keyboard focus, closing the gap.

## Requirement Consistency — Error Handling Across Flows

- [x] CHK010 Do the four failure-path requirements (chat FR-007, upload FR-011, download FR-014,
      delete FR-017) apply the same standard of specificity — one distinct, human-readable message
      per distinct backend failure cause — or does FR-011/FR-014's "a specific/clear message" leave
      more implementation latitude than FR-007's explicitly enumerated retry guarantee? [Consistency,
      Spec §FR-007/FR-011/FR-014/FR-017] — **Fixed**: all four now explicitly require a distinct
      message per distinct documented failure cause.
- [x] CHK011 Is retry guidance stated with equal explicitness for every failure path — FR-007
      explicitly says the user "can try again," FR-011 says the control is "usable for another
      attempt," but does FR-014 (download) or FR-017 (delete) state whether/how the same action can
      be retried after a failure? [Consistency, Gap, Spec §FR-014/FR-017] — **Fixed**: FR-014/FR-017
      now state persistence/retry expectations explicitly; SC-005 states retry applies to every
      failure case except a download against a permanently-deleted document.
- [x] CHK012 Is the placement/scope of an error message (inline at the point of the failed action, a
      row-local indicator, or a page/conversation-level notice) specified consistently, or left to
      vary per flow with no stated rationale? [Consistency, Gap, Spec §FR-007/FR-011/FR-014/FR-017] —
      **Fixed**: each FR now states where its message appears (in place of the pending answer, at the
      upload control, at the download trigger, at the document's row).
- [x] CHK013 Does the spec state whether a failed chat request remains visible as a distinct entry in
      the conversation history (FR-018), or is silently retried in place — an interaction between
      FR-007 and FR-018 that isn't explicitly resolved? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007/FR-018] — **Fixed**:
      FR-007/FR-018 now state the failed entry stays in history; retry is a new question.

## Requirement Completeness — Error Handling & Failure Modes

- [x] CHK014 Are requirements defined for what the user sees if two independent failures occur close
      together (e.g. a chat request fails while a delete confirmation on an unrelated document is
      also pending)? [Gap, Coverage] — **Fixed**: new FR-022 requires chat/upload/delete-confirmation
      states to be mutually independent.
- [x] CHK015 Is there a requirement covering an upload that fails partway through transmission (e.g.
      network drop mid-upload), distinct from a clean rejection response — or is this treated
      identically to any other "service could not process it" case? [Gap, Spec §FR-011] — **Fixed**:
      FR-011 now states a mid-upload network failure is treated the same as a service-unavailable
      rejection.
- [x] CHK016 Are requirements defined for a download failure that is not a `404` (e.g. the backend is
      unreachable entirely during a download attempt), distinct from FR-014's specifically-scoped
      "document no longer exists" case? [Gap, Coverage, Spec §FR-014] — **Fixed**: FR-014 now covers
      "any other failure" alongside the 404 case.
- [x] CHK017 Does the spec define whether an error state (chat, upload, download, or delete) is
      automatically cleared by the user's next unrelated action, or persists until explicitly
      dismissed or retried? [Gap, Spec §FR-007/FR-011/FR-014/FR-017] — **Fixed**: all four FRs now
      state their error state's persistence/clearing condition explicitly.

## Scenario Coverage — Edge Cases & Concurrent Flows

- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for triggering a second document's delete confirmation while a
      first document's delete confirmation is still open and unconfirmed? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec
      §FR-015] — **Fixed**: new FR-021 + an Edge Cases entry resolve this (only one open at a time).
- [x] CHK019 Are requirements defined for attempting to delete a document while an upload is still in
      progress, or attempting an upload while a delete confirmation is open? [Gap, Edge Case] —
      **Fixed**: new FR-022 + an Edge Cases entry (the three areas are independent).
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for a document being deleted (by this or, hypothetically,
      another concurrent client) while it is still listed in the sidebar the current user is looking
      at, beyond the already-covered citation-download case (Edge Cases, Spec)? [Gap, Coverage] —
      **Fixed**: a new Assumptions bullet scopes multi-tab/concurrent-client races explicitly.
- [x] CHK021 Does the edge-case list address a user navigating away (reload/close tab) while an
      upload or delete request is still in flight — is the outcome (completed server-side but not
      reflected client-side) an accepted, documented gap? [Gap, Edge Case] — **Fixed**: a new Edge
      Cases entry + Assumptions bullet document this explicitly.

## Non-Hover / Keyboard Interaction Coverage

- [x] CHK022 Since FR-013 and FR-015 phrase the sidebar's download and delete actions as a "hover
      action," are equivalent requirements defined for a user who cannot hover (keyboard-only or
      touch-only interaction), or is this explicitly deferred? [Gap, Coverage, Spec §FR-013/FR-015] —
      **Fixed**: FR-013 now requires keyboard-focus reachability; Story 4/5 each gained an explicit
      keyboard acceptance scenario.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK023 Is SC-005's "leaves the user with a clear next action" objectively verifiable per
      failure case, or does it rely on subjective judgment of what counts as "clear"? [Measurability,
      Spec §SC-005] — **Fixed**: SC-005 now states a concrete, checkable pair of criteria (a specific
      pre-defined message; retry available except for the one named exception).
- [x] CHK024 Are the four failure categories SC-005 enumerates (invalid question, upload rejected,
      delete failed, backend unreachable) a complete list against the failure paths defined
      elsewhere in the spec (e.g. does it omit the download-failure case FR-014 defines)?
      [Completeness, Consistency, Spec §SC-005/FR-014] — **Fixed**: SC-005 now includes download
      failure in its enumerated list.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK025 Is the feature's dependency on a backend CORS change (beyond what already exists for
      `/actuator/health`) — without which no request in any user story can reach the backend at all
      — documented anywhere in the spec's Assumptions? [Gap, Dependency, Spec §Assumptions] —
      **Fixed**: a new Assumptions bullet documents this dependency explicitly.
- [x] CHK026 Is the acceptance of an unbounded wait for a chat response (no client-side timeout, per
      the Clarifications session) reflected as an explicit assumption/risk, given SC-001's "no
      dead-end" expectation could otherwise read as contradicting an indefinite wait? [Consistency,
      Spec §Clarifications/SC-001] — **Fixed**: a new Assumptions bullet reconciles the two
      explicitly.
